Senses.Explanation: This interrogative asks how something is, how one will respond, or what can be said or done: “how?” Its force is often a live demand rather than a request for exposition. Baizhang Huaihai blocks throat and lips and asks how Guishan will speak; Shitou Xiqian rejects “this way” and “not this way” and asks what his student will do; Linji Yixuan asks how the present listener proposes to cultivate, realize, or adorn the person hearing the teaching. It also follows a proposed action—“what if the foot is raised?”—asks how someone understands a case, presses “ultimately, how?”, asks how a ceremonial address should be raised, or introduces “what is the final phrase?” Dialectal spellings perform the same interrogative work in the stored witnesses. The phrase supplies no answer by itself; its recurring role is to force the next move.
Senses.Note: Exact frozen-corpus count: 29,839 hits in 443 files and 436 works. Ten curated occurrences cover personal, modal, interpretive, ceremonial, and case-question frames.
